findings.title: Costs
findings.text: Slippage and commissions cost 0.017R per trade on average (-0.001R before costs, -0.019R after). Costs turn a small loss into a bigger one; they are not the main reason for losing.

findings.title: Win rate vs what's needed
findings.text: Win rate 47.2% against about 49.2% needed to break even with the actual average winner (+0.48R) and loser (-0.47R). Median target was 3.0R; only 1.7% of trades ever reached +2R before exiting.

findings.title: False breakouts
findings.text: 69.8% of stopped trades were stopped within 2 bars of entry: the move reversed almost immediately. That is a lot of instant failures, typical of breakouts in choppy markets.

findings.title: Giving back winners
findings.text: 1.3% of losing trades were up at least +1R at some point before turning into a loss. Few losers were ever meaningfully profitable, so exit management isn't the main problem.

findings.title: Stop placement
findings.text: 0.0% of stopped trades went on to reach the original target later the same day. Wider stops mean smaller positions, so this is a trade-off to test, not a fix.

findings.title: Long vs short
findings.text: Best: short -0.003R over 1333 trades (95% interval [-0.07, 0.06]). Worst: long -0.033R over 1461 trades (interval [-0.079, 0.014]).

findings.title: Trading with or against the trend
findings.text: Best: with trend +0.011R over 1504 trades (95% interval [-0.044, 0.065]). Worst: no clear trend -0.135R over 194 trades (interval [-0.214, -0.053]).

findings.title: Time of day
findings.text: Best: 11:30-14:00 midday +0.026R over 894 trades (95% interval [-0.025, 0.075]). Worst: 10:00-11:30 morning -0.047R over 1683 trades (interval [-0.099, 0.009]).

findings.title: Choppy markets
findings.text: Best: choppy / consolidating +0.017R over 104 trades (95% interval [-0.116, 0.147]). Worst: trending / expanding -0.020R over 2690 trades (interval [-0.056, 0.017]).

findings.title: Late / extended entries
findings.text: Best: near 9 EMA (<=1.5 ATR) -0.010R over 2014 trades (95% interval [-0.051, 0.035]). Worst: extended (>1.5 ATR from 9 EMA) -0.043R over 780 trades (interval [-0.095, 0.01]).

findings.title: Volume confirmation
findings.text: Best: volume confirmed -0.009R over 685 trades (95% interval [-0.062, 0.043]). Worst: weak volume -0.022R over 2109 trades (interval [-0.06, 0.017]).

findings.title: Volatility
findings.text: Best: high-vol +0.016R over 599 trades (95% interval [-0.076, 0.123]). Worst: normal-vol -0.028R over 2195 trades (interval [-0.062, 0.006]).

findings.title: Checklist score
findings.text: Best: checklist >= 70 +0.006R over 662 trades (95% interval [-0.059, 0.073]). Worst: checklist < 50 -0.044R over 1042 trades (interval [-0.088, 0.002]).

findings.title: Setups with positive evidence
findings.text: None. No setup or ticker slice has an out-of-sample 95% interval entirely above zero.

diagnostics.caveat: These slices describe past out-of-sample trades. Choosing filters from them and re-testing on the same trades would be curve-fitting; any idea here must be confirmed on later data.

search.note: Each fold tried 12 parameter combinations on its training window and kept the best. The more combinations tried, the more the training winner is a lucky draw - which is exactly why only the following, unseen test window is reported.
